source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Selecting good seed is the first key technique for successful watermelon cultivation. Farmers commonly use three general seed types: local/open-pollinated seed, cross-pollinated seed, and hybrid F1 seed. Hybrid F1 seed is recommended because, although it costs more than ordinary seed, it produces plants that are stronger, more resistant to disease, and give a higher and more uniform yield, so the extra seed cost is offset by better returns.

Good seed should be obtained from a reliable, reputable source (a trusted seed company or seed shop) and should show a high germination rate, ideally above 85 percent. Seed should be plump, uniform in size, free of visible damage, insect holes, or mold, and free of disease. Farmers are advised to check the germination test result and the expiry/production date printed on the seed packet before buying, and to avoid seed that has been stored a long time or improperly stored, since this reduces germination and seedling vigor.
